subject: food-technology
title: Vegan, Vegetarian and Plant-Based
welcome_lead: From flexitarian to fully plant-based — diet trends and nutrition planning.
meta_desc: A-Level Food Tech: vegan and vegetarian nutrition.

concepts.def: Excludes all animal products, including dairy and eggs.
Excludes meat and fish; may include dairy and eggs.
Eats dairy and eggs; no meat or fish.
Combining plant sources to supply all essential amino acids.
Vitamin only reliably found in animal products or fortified foods.
Food with added nutrients (e.g. plant milk + B12 + calcium).

walkthroughs.body_html: Vegan: no animal products. Lacto-ovo vegetarian: dairy and eggs OK. Pescetarian: includes fish. Flexitarian: mostly plant-based with occasional animal foods.
Vegan diets need attention to B12 (fortified plant milks or supplement), iron (non-haem, less bioavailable — pair with vitamin C), iodine, omega-3 (algae oil), calcium, and protein quality.

Most plant proteins lack one or more essential amino acids. Complementary proteins: beans + rice, hummus + pitta, peanut butter + bread. Across a day's intake — not single meal — sufficient mix is achieved.
